content.comment_body: About five years ago, I manually installed [product_name] version [version_no] on Arch Linux (and also on Debian/Ubuntu). I avoided the 'native' installer provided by [company_name], since it doesn't proceed on non-SUSE or non-openSUSE systems. Instead, I manually set up [product_name] and documented the process in a step-by-step guide for installing [product_name] on non-SUSE Linux distributions, which I posted on this forum (see [url]). Over the years, I've continued using [product_name] [version_no], although I haven't installed new hardware recently. Now that I am working on a fresh project, I would like to upgrade and use [product_name] [version_no]. Unfortunately, [company_name] only supplies a Setup.bin script for the upgrade, but this script doesn't accommodate non-SUSE distributions or provide the necessary files for manual updating in the /opt/[product_name] directory where my current version resides. I prefer not to pay for the latest minor update since [company_name] allows upgrading. Could anyone guide me on where I can obtain the files needed to swap out my old executables for the latest ones? I'd appreciate your advice. Best regards, [user_name].

[SOLVED] My mistake—I forgot to set directory permissions to 755. Eventually, [company_name] technical support ([url]) sent me a copy of [product_name] [version_no], which enabled me to update my previous installation. By reusing my own step-by-step guide (referenced in my earlier post), I installed [product_name] [version_no] in /opt/[product_name][version_no], next to the old /opt/[product_name][version_no]. However, when launching /opt/[product_name][version_no]/Application_64/[product_name], the application fails to start, displaying errors related to the Java environment: Unable to locate the application's 'main' class. The class 'Start' must be public and contain a 'public static void main(String[])' method. My older [product_name] [version_no] continues to work without issues. I believe this failure in [version_no] is tied to the Java virtual machine embedded with this version, not to the installation method. To my knowledge, [product_name] includes its own Java VM and doesn't rely on the system's JRE. Has anyone using Linux (other than SUSE) experienced this problem? I welcome your feedback. Best regards, [user_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter major challenges when installing or upgrading newer [product_name] versions on Linux distributions not officially supported by [company_name], due to installation scripts failing and software depending on bundled Java environments. Manual installation approaches succeed with older releases, but current versions yield errors at startup linked to Java class configuration. These obstacles highlight persistent compatibility issues for Linux users outside SUSE/openSUSE ecosystems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope [company_name] will supply direct upgrade files or instructions facilitating manual installation of [product_name] on non-SUSE Linux distributions, enabling hassle-free use of updated software without unnecessary purchases or unsupported installer tools.
